14149-the-pilots-of-pomona-a-story-of-th.title: A Story of the Orkney Islands
14149-the-pilots-of-pomona-a-story-of-th.creator: Robert Leighton
14149-the-pilots-of-pomona-a-story-of-th.description: A book by Robert Leighton. On a certain bright morning in the month of May, 1843, the little port of Stromness wore an aspect of unwonted commotion. The great whaling fleet that every year sailed from this place for the Greenland fisheries was busily preparing for sea. The sun was shining over the brown hills of Orphir, and casting a golden sheen over the calm bay.

arxiv-2105-13772.title: High-Energy Standard Model from the Gauge Group Contraction
arxiv-2105-13772.description: Abstract The evolution of properties and interactions of elementary particles, beginning with the Planck scale of 10 19 10^{19} GeV. The description is based on the hypothesis that the high-temperature (high-energy) limit of the Standard Model is generated by the gauge group contraction.

arxiv-2110-14380.title: Revisiting a Low-Dimensional Model with Short Range Interactions and Mean Field Critical Behavior
arxiv-2110-14380.creator: Peter Grassberger
arxiv-2110-14380.description: Abstract In all local low-dimensional models, scaling at critical points deviates from mean field behavior – with one possible exception. This exceptional model with “ordinary” behavior is an inherently non-equilibrium model studied some time ago by H.-M. Bröker and myself. In simulations, its 2-dimensional version suggested that two critical exponents were mean-field, while a third one showed very small deviations.

arxiv-2205-10316.title: Complex behavior from intrinsic motivation to occupy future action-state path space
arxiv-2205-10316.creator: Jorge Ramírez-Ruiz, Dmytro Grytskyy, Chiara Mastrogiuseppe, Yamen Habib, Rubén Moreno-Bote
arxiv-2205-10316.description: Abstract Most theories of behavior posit that agents tend to maximize some form of reward or utility. However, animals very often move with curiosity and seem to be motivated in a reward-free manner. Here we abandon the idea of reward maximization, and propose that the goal of behavior is maximizing occupancy of future paths of actions and states.

arxiv-2210-09257.title: Turbocharging Solution Concepts: Solving NEs, CEs and CCEs with Neural Equilibrium Solvers
arxiv-2210-09257.creator: Luke Marris, Ian Gemp, Thomas Anthony, Andrea Tacchetti, Siqi Liu, Karl Tuyls
arxiv-2210-09257.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Luke Marris, Ian Gemp, Thomas Anthony, Andrea Tacchetti, Siqi Liu, Karl Tuyls. Solution concepts such as Nash Equilibria, Correlated Equilibria, and Coarse Correlated Equilibria are useful components for many multiagent machine learning algorithms. Unfortunately, solving a normal-form game could take prohibitive or non-deterministic time to converge, and could fail. We introduce the Neural Equilibrium Solver which utilizes a special equivariant neural network architecture to approximately solve the space of all games of fixed shape, buying speed and determinism.

arxiv-2310-01685.title: A Framework for Interpretability in Machine Learning for Medical Imaging
arxiv-2310-01685.creator: ALAN Q. WANG 1,2, BATUHAN K. KARAMAN 1,2, HEEJONG KIM 2, JACOB ROSENTHAL 2,3, RACHIT SALUJA 1,2, SEAN I. YOUNG 4,5, MERT R. SABUNCU 1,2
arxiv-2310-01685.description: Abstract Interpretability for machine learning models in medical imaging (MLMI) is an important direction of research. However, there is a general sense of murkiness in what interpretability means. Why does the need for interpretability in MLMI arise? What goals does one actually seek to address when interpretability is needed?

arxiv-2310-16766.title: Conditional Euclidean distance optimization via relative tangency
arxiv-2310-16766.creator: Sandra Di Rocco, Lukas Gustafsson, Luca Sodomaco
arxiv-2310-16766.description: Abstract . We introduce a theory of relative tangency for projective algebraic varieties. The dual variety X Z ∨ X_{Z}^{\vee} of a variety X X relative to a subvariety Z Z is the set of hyperplanes tangent to X X at a point of Z Z .

arxiv-2311-01327.title: High-dimensional Linear Bandits with Knapsacks
arxiv-2311-01327.creator: Wanteng Ma † \text{Wanteng Ma}^{\dagger} Dong Xia † \text{Dong Xia}^{\dagger} Jiashuo Jiang ‡ \text{Jiashuo Jiang}^{\ddagger}
arxiv-2311-01327.description: Abstract We study the contextual bandits with knapsack (CBwK) problem under the high-dimensional setting where the dimension of the feature is large. The reward of pulling each arm equals the multiplication of a sparse high-dimensional weight vector and the feature of the current arrival, with additional random noise.

arxiv-2311-07978.title: AfroBench: How Good are Large Language Models on African Languages?
arxiv-2311-07978.creator: Jessica Ojo, Odunayo Ogundepo, Akintunde Oladipo, Kelechi Ogueji, Jimmy Lin, Pontus Stenetorp, David Ifeoluwa Adelani .
arxiv-2311-07978.description: Abstract Large-scale multilingual evaluations, such as MEGA, often include only a handful of African languages due to the scarcity of high-quality evaluation data and the limited discoverability of existing African datasets. This lack of representation hinders comprehensive LLM evaluation across a diverse range of languages and tasks.

arxiv-2404-17260.title: The evolution of the Permutahedron
arxiv-2404-17260.creator: Maurício Collares, Joseph Doolittle, Joshua Erde
arxiv-2404-17260.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Maurício Collares, Joseph Doolittle, Joshua Erde. In their seminal paper introducing the theory of random graphs, Erdős and Rényi considered the evolution of the structure of a random subgraph of K n K_{n} as the density increases from 0 0 to 1 1 , identifying two key points in this evolution – the percolation threshold , where the order of the largest component seemingly jumps from logarithmic to linear in size, and the connectivity threshold , where the subgraph becomes connected.

arxiv-2509-18728.title: The inside-out quenching of the MHONGOOSE galaxy NGC 1371
arxiv-2509-18728.creator: S. Veronese, W. J. G. de Blok, F. Fraternali, F. M. Maccagni, J. Healy, D. Kleiner, T. A. Oosterloo, R. Morganti
arxiv-2509-18728.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by S. Veronese, W. J. G. de Blok, F. Fraternali, F. M. Maccagni, J. Healy, D. Kleiner, T. A. Oosterloo, R. Morganti. We present the deepest 21-cm spectral line and 1.4 GHz broad-band continuum observations of nearby early-type spiral galaxy NGC 1371 as part of the MeerKAT H i Observations of Nearby Galactic Objects: Observing Southern Emitters (MHONGOOSE) survey.

arxiv-2602-12128.title: HLA: Hadamard Linear Attention
arxiv-2602-12128.creator: Hanno Ackermann, Hong Cai, Mohsen Ghafoorian, Amirhossein Habibian, Qualcomm AI Research
arxiv-2602-12128.description: Abstract The attention mechanism is an important reason for the success of transformers. It relies on computing pairwise relations between tokens. To reduce the high computational cost of standard quadratic attention, linear attention has been proposed as an efficient approximation. It employs kernel functions that are applied independently to the inputs before the pairwise similarities are calculated.

arxiv-2602-20341.title: The Tragedy of Chain Commons CCS: Security and privacy Distributed systems security CCS: Applied computing Electronic commerce
arxiv-2602-20341.creator: Ignacio Amores-Sesar, Mirza Ahad Baig, Seth Gilbert, Ray Neiheiser, Michelle X. Yeo
arxiv-2602-20341.description: Abstract . Byzantine Fault Tolerant (BFT) consensus forms the foundation of many modern blockchains striving for both high throughput and low latency. A growing bottleneck is transaction execution and validation on the critical path of consensus, which has led to modular decoupled designs that separate ordering from execution: consensus orders only metadata, while transactions are executed and validated concurrently.

plos-pone-0348221.creator: Apisith Saraluck, Orawee Chinthakanan, Komkrit Aimjirakul, Rujira Wattanayingcharoenchai, Jittima Manonai

pmc-10559690.title: Leucocytoclastic Vasculitis Presenting as Bilateral Ulcerative Keratitis: A Case Report
pmc-10559690.creator: Hui Feng, Shang Li, Ying Jie
pmc-10559690.description: Introduction:Small artery disease caused by neutrophils and immune-mediated is known as leucocytoclastic vasculitis (LCV). Clinically, it manifests as palpable, asymptomatic purpuric papules on the limbs. Ocular manifestation is rare. Here, we describe a case of peripheral ulcerative keratitis (PUK) associated with LCV.

pmc-11356779.title: Is There a Pathologic Running Motion Associated with Running-Related Injuries? A Methodological Study Using a Motion Analysis System Without Sensors
pmc-11356779.creator: Hyok Woo Nam, Jae Hyuk Yang, Seul Gi Park, Hye Chang Rhim, Hong Jin Kim, Nicola Luigi Bragazzi
pmc-11356779.description: (1) Background and objectives: Running-related injuries (RRIs) are commonly attributed to improper running posture and overuse. This study aims to analyze the running motions of individuals with and without RRIs using a sensor-free method, which offers a user-friendly and straightforward approach.

pmc-11476325.title: Advances in Cancer Therapy: A Comprehensive Review of CDK and EGFR Inhibitors
pmc-11476325.creator: Mohammed Hawash, Zamal Ahmed, John A Tainer
pmc-11476325.description: Protein kinases have essential responsibilities in controlling several cellular processes, and their abnormal regulation is strongly related to the development of cancer. The implementation of protein kinase inhibitors has significantly transformed cancer therapy by modifying treatment strategies. These inhibitors have received substantial FDA clearance in recent decades.

pmc-11531161.title: Effects of systemic ventricular assist in failing Fontan patients: a theoretical analysis using a computational model
pmc-11531161.creator: Eiri Kisamori, Yasuhiro Kotani, Toshiaki Shishido, Shingo Kasahara, Shuji Shimizu
pmc-11531161.description: Mechanical circulatory support is a potential treatment for failing Fontan patients. In this study, we performed a theoretical analysis using a computational model to clarify the effects of systemic ventricular assist device (VAD) in failing Fontan patients. Cardiac chambers and vascular systems were described using the time-varying elastance model and modified Windkessel model, respectively.

pmc-11788303.title: Features and evolutionary adaptations of the mitochondrial genome of Garuga forrestii W. W. Sm
pmc-11788303.creator: Rong Chen, Rui Rao, Chun Wang, Dongbo Zhu, Fen Yuan, Liangliang Yue
pmc-11788303.description: Introduction Garuga forrestii W. W. Sm. is a tree species of the Burseraceae family, endemic to China, found in hot/warm-dry valleys. This species plays a crucial role in maintaining biodiversity in these ecosystems.MethodsWe performed de novo assembly of the Garuga forrestii mitochondrial genome using PMAT (v.1.5.4), resulting in a typical circular molecule of 606,853 bp.

pmc-11794456.title: DeepPFP: a multi-task-aware architecture for protein function prediction
pmc-11794456.creator: Han Wang, Zilin Ren, Jinghong Sun, Yongbing Chen, Xiaochen Bo, JiGuo Xue, Jingyang Gao, Ming Ni
pmc-11794456.description: Deriving protein function from protein sequences poses a significant challenge due to the intricate relationship between sequence and function. Deep learning has made remarkable strides in predicting sequence-function relationships. However, models tailored for specific tasks or protein types encounter difficulties when using transfer learning across domains.

pmc-12364795.title: Five advanced chatbots solving European Diploma in Radiology (EDiR) text-based questions: differences in performance and consistency
pmc-12364795.creator: Jakub Pristoupil, Laura Oleaga, Vanesa Junquero, Cristina Merino, Suha Sureyya Ozbek, Lukas Lambert, European Society of Radiology (ESR)
pmc-12364795.description: BackgroundWe compared the performance, confidence, and response consistency of five chatbots powered by large language models in solving European Diploma in Radiology (EDiR) text-based multiple-response questions.MethodsChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-4o-mini, Copilot, Gemini, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet were tested using 52 text-based multiple-response questions from two previous EDiR sessions in two iterations.

pmc-12408723.title: A systematic review of protein post-translational modifications in sepsis
pmc-12408723.creator: Lishun Yang, Zhuang’e Shi, Fuping Wang, Guoyun Shi, Couwen Li, Guobing Chen
pmc-12408723.description: BackgroundSepsis originates from the host's dysregulated response to pathogens, and its pathophysiological mechanisms are extremely complex. Recent research has found that post-translational modifications (PTMs) can regulate gene transcription without altering the genetic sequence, thereby playing a key role in the occurrence and development of sepsis.

pmc-12610027.title: Pulsatilla Saponin D Suppresses Proliferation and Induces Apoptosis in Human Prostatic Cells
pmc-12610027.creator: Yuzhong Chen, Ping Zhou, Yangtao Jin, Dongyan Huang, Xin Su, Congcong Shao, Juan Jiang, Rongfu Yang, Jianhui Wu
pmc-12610027.description: The growing global aging population is contributing to an increasing burden of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), highlighting the need for novel, highly effective and low-toxicity therapies. In light of its well-documented anti-inflammatory and anti-tumor properties, we investigated the potential of the natural product Pulsatilla saponin D (PSD) in treating BPH.

pmc-12708689.title: Traditional clothing pattern extraction considering attention mechanism and image data enhancement processing
pmc-12708689.creator: Dandan He, Bing Xia, Hong Li
pmc-12708689.description: The three core challenges faced in traditional clothing pattern extraction are poor image quality, complex texture, and scarcity of labeled data. To solve these problems, the study proposes a multi-scale data augmentation with polarized self-attention for traditional costume pattern extraction.

pmc-13027808.title: Cutaneous Fungal Infections in Greek Competitive Swimmers: A Cross-Sectional, Self-Reported Study
pmc-13027808.creator: Eleni Sfyri, Niki Tertipi, Vasiliki-Sofia Grech, Vasiliki Kefala, Efstathios Rallis
pmc-13027808.description: Background/Objectives: Cutaneous fungal infections, specifically tinea pedis, pityriasis versicolor, and tinea unguium (onychomycosis), are common yet under-researched in swimming. This study aimed to evaluate their prevalence and associated risk factors among competitive swimmers in Greece. Methods: An anonymous questionnaire was administered to 1047 participants, comprising parents of minor swimmers and adult athletes.

pmc-13320570.title: The Outcome of Double Antibiotic, Triple Antibiotic, and Modified Triple Antibiotic Pastes as an Intracanal Medicament in Regenerative Endodontics: A Comparative Study
pmc-13320570.creator: Takhellambam P Devi, Shamurailatpam Priyadarshini, Kangjam G Singh, Deepak B Suryakanth, Jenny Atom, Sagolsem Chandarani
pmc-13320570.description: BackgroundAntibiotic paste plays a vital role in the success of regenerative endodontics. Triple antibiotic paste (TAP) and double antibiotic paste (DAP) are commonly used as intracanal medicaments, with tooth discoloration being a main concern for TAP. Clindamycin is a broad-spectrum antibiotic and does not cause visible tooth discoloration.

pmc-13332630.title: Long-Term Follow-Up After Dual Transcatheter Valve-in-Valve Implantation Under VA-ECMO Support
pmc-13332630.creator: Raghuram Palaparti, Max Lenz, Varius Dannenberg, Gregor Heitzinger, Caglayan Demirel, Anna Bartunek, Christian Nitsche, Luliana Coti, Irene Lang, Philipp E Bartko
pmc-13332630.description: BackgroundCardiogenic shock due to simultaneous degeneration of multiple prosthetic valves is rare and is associated with prohibitive surgical risk.Case SummaryA 73-year-old woman with 3 prior sternotomies presented with acute decompensated heart failure, which rapidly progressed to cardiogenic shock after atrial fibrillation. Multimodality imaging demonstrated severe dysfunction of both aortic and mitral bioprostheses, with biventricular dysfunction.

pmc-13537446.title: Case of implant failure following osteosynthesis for an intertrochanteric femoral fracture using a carbon fiber intramedullary nail
pmc-13537446.creator: Taisei Suzuki, Shigeo Fukunishi, Shohei Okahisa, Saori Niitsu, Syuya Matsumoto, Toshiya Tachibana
pmc-13537446.description: Carbon fiber-reinforced polyetheretherketone (CFR-PEEK) materials are radiolucent and produce fewer metallic artifacts during radiological examinations, making them a subject of growing interest as osteosynthesis materials in the field of orthopedics. However, clinical reports on carbon intramedullary nails are still limited, and there are few reports on postoperative complications.
